title: Token refresh before publish (M0.8)
head: lead/token-refresh
body:
Stacked on #7. Closes M0.8 (pre-publish refresh; the remainder of M1.6 is tracked in the roadmap).

An expiring token used to fail the publish — fatal for short-lived platforms (TikTok issues 24h tokens). The worker now refreshes **before** sending.

**New `src/lib/adapters/tokens.ts`** — `needsTokenRefresh(expiresAt, now, skew)` and `canRefresh(hasRefreshToken, platformSupportsRefresh)`, both pure so the policy is testable without a platform. Refresh happens 5 minutes ahead of nominal expiry so a publish never races the clock; a token with no recorded expiry (Telegram bot tokens) is never treated as expired.

**Worker behaviour:**
- expiring and refreshable -> refresh, persist the new encrypted token + expiry, then publish with it
- expiring but NOT refreshable (no refresh token, or a connector whose tokens never refresh) -> dead-letter on attempt 1 as `AUTH_EXPIRED`, telling the operator to reconnect
- refresh call itself fails -> the failure is classified like any other, so an unreachable platform backs off and retries while bad credentials dead-letter immediately

**Verification:**

```
npm run typecheck     -> clean
npm run test:unit     -> # tests 28 | # pass 28 | # fail 0   (7 new token-lifetime assertions)
npm run test:durability -> 24/24
  CASE D expired token on a non-refreshable connector
    [PASS] not retried            [PASS] dead-letters on attempt 1
    [PASS] classified AUTH_EXPIRED, not a generic failure
    [PASS] operator is told what to do ("reconnect the account")
    [PASS] post ends FAILED
```

Cases A (transient), B (permanent) and C (dedupe) still pass unchanged.
